HEDGE FUNDS DUMP TECH STOCKS AT FASTEST PACE IN A DECADE Goldman Sachs reports that hedge funds cut technology exposure at the fastest pace since at least 2016 during the five sessions ending October 15. Despite the selloff, tech still represents 23.5% of hedge fund portfolios, near historically elevated levels.

U.S. PENDING HOME SALES PLUNGE 7.3% IN SEPTEMBER U.S. pending home sales fell 7.3% month-over-month in September, reversing August's modest 0.3% gain. The index dropped to 66.0, with sales down 11.3% year-over-year. All four regions weakened, led by the West (-9.2%) and South (-8.2%).

CITADEL’S KEN GRIFFIN: WE’RE ALMOST CERTAINLY IN AN AI BUBBLE Billionaire Ken Griffin warns investors are “almost certainly” in an AI bubble, as companies struggle to turn massive AI spending into measurable productivity gains. With Anthropic reportedly eyeing $750 billion in future computing expenditures, questions over AI investment returns are intensifying. But Griffin remains bullish on AI’s long-term potential.

SPCX - JPMORGAN DOUBLES SPACEX PRICE TARGET TO $500 JPMorgan raised its SpaceX price target from $240 to $500, maintaining an Overweight rating. The bank now forecasts $254 billion in 2027 revenue and 10 GW of computing capacity by year-end, more than doubling its 2027–2028 estimates. JPMorgan also sees strategic merit in a potential SpaceX–Tesla merger, though no deal is guaranteed.

YARDENI: THE AI BUBBLE IS REAL, BUT NOT READY TO BURST Yardeni Research's new AI Bubble Meter flashes a warning, but not a crash signal. Bubble Conditions stand at 83/100, while Crash Triggers remain at just 34/100. Historically, similar conditions preceded an S&P 500 bear market only 9% of the time within two years, with a median inflation-adjusted gain of 18.3%. The key takeaway: AI valuations look stretched, but the forces needed to burst the bubble haven't fully materialized.

OPENAI AND GOOGLE STRIKE MAJOR AI DISTRIBUTION DEAL OpenAI will bring its frontier AI models, including GPT-6 Astra, and Codex to Google Cloud in the coming weeks. Enterprise customers will be able to purchase them through Google Cloud Marketplace, using existing cloud spending commitments. The agreement follows OpenAI's expansion to AWS after its exclusive Microsoft distribution arrangement ended.

MORE OIL IS LEAVING THE PERSIAN GULF THAN BEFORE THE WAR Middle East oil exports exceeded prewar levels in the week through October 18, according to Kpler. A U.S.-protected shipping system is keeping tankers moving despite continued attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Yet oil prices remain elevated as shipping costs surge, inventories tighten and traders fear renewed escalation.

U.S. TAPS EMERGENCY DIESEL RESERVE AS PRICES HIT $6.32 The Trump administration will release 315,000 barrels from the Northeast's 1 million-barrel heating oil reserve as diesel prices surge ahead of the midterm elections. Diesel now averages $6.32 per gallon, according to AAA, amid disruptions linked to the Iran war. Deliveries are expected by November 13. The key takeaway: Washington is tapping emergency fuel supplies to ease pressure from soaring energy costs.

U.S. CRUDE INVENTORIES PLUNGE, FAR EXCEEDING EXPECTATIONS U.S. crude oil inventories fell 3.06 million barrels last week, versus expectations for a decline of just 324,000 barrels. 🔸 Crude stocks: 412.5M barrels, 3% below normal 🔸 Gasoline inventories: -3.0M barrels 🔸 Distillate inventories: +1.7M barrels 🔸 Total petroleum inventories: -8.5M barrels The key takeaway: A much larger-than-expected inventory draw signals tighter U.S. oil supplies, adding potential upward pressure on crude prices.
